machine.shared: A development machine, with other work running at times; the A/B runs are alternated for that reason

build.tls: OpenSSL 3.6.5 (bundled, static: linux-ext-libs 1.24, both sides); mbedTLS not built on this machine
build.note: CONFIG_DEBUG_TRACK_MEMORY is on (the .config of this machine): every allocation is tracked. A build without it does less work per allocation; that build was not measured here.

method.ab: Written on 2026-10-22, after the release, and against 7.27.0: the last release with a study. It replaces the study written the day before, which compared 7.27.5 with 7.27.4, a release nobody had measured. This one covers 7.27.1 to 7.27.5. 7.27.0 and 7.27.5 each built from a git worktree of its tag, with the same .config and compiler; in each tree only the kernel libraries, the modules, performance/c/ and the three ctest binaries were built, and the perf_timeranger2 of the main tree (with its `read` phase, public API only) was compiled into both. outputs_ext was shared (linux-ext-libs 1.24, OpenSSL 3.6.5 and PCRE2 10.49): 7.27.0 shipped with 1.23 (OpenSSL 3.6.3), and that change of 7.27.1 is not in these figures; it was measured on its own when 7.27.1 shipped (no move: the TLS echo -0.9%, t = -0.6). The two binaries of each benchmark run alternately, the order flipped every round, with a sync and a 3 s pause before each run (1 s for the three ctest binaries and the read phase): 16 rounds; 24 for perf_timeranger2 and perf_tr_treedb, run with 7.27.4 in a rotation of three; 48 for the `read` phase alone (the last 24 with 7.27.4 in the rotation). perf_rotatory 16 rounds, its 9th left out: something on the machine slowed both builds alike for that minute (a log line 1.5 times its time on both). To place each move in its release, the `read` phase ran once more, 24 rounds, on every tag from 7.27.0 to 7.27.5 and on two commits of 7.27.5 (bd3fdce51, its first, and 83a771089). Mean +- standard deviation (median), t = the change over its standard error; |t| < 3 is noise. The treedb figures are CPU time of the process per operation.
method.tag_run: The absolute figures of 7.27.5 are its side of this A/B run: the code of the tag, built on 2026-10-22 from a worktree of the tag on the machine of the earlier reports. Not a tag-time run: the release was tagged on 2026-10-21 without one. The per-second benchmarks drop their first and last second; reads page by page are the FORWARD pass. The binary sizes are those of a build of the tag made the same day for the first study.

story.title: Yuneta 7.27.5: retention, and what it costs a replica to read
story.lead: 7.27.5 gives timeranger2 retention: a store deletes the old files of a key and keeps the `g_rowid` of every row that stays, and its followers hear the purge. This study compares it with 7.27.0, the last release with a study, so it covers 7.27.1 to 7.27.5 together, and every move is placed in the release where it appeared by building the tags between them. It replaces the one written the day after the release against 7.27.4, a release nobody had measured. A replica pays about 1 us more for every iterator open and every page, purged or not: one `stat()` that notices a purge whose signal it missed. That is +18% on a page of one row, +7% on an open; the master does not pay it. It appeared in 7.27.5, with commit 83a771089. A page of 100 rows costs 1.5% more (the base of the key read for every row), and a forced treedb delete 3.9% more. Everything else from 7.27.1 to 7.27.5, the gobj and TCP changes of 7.27.2 to 7.27.4 among them, moves inside its noise.

hero.text: more per iterator open and per page on a replica: the price of noticing a purge it did not hear. It appeared in 7.27.5 (commit 83a771089); 7.27.1 to 7.27.4 read at 7.27.0's speed, and the master does not pay it.

A forced delete removes the node's key (tranger2_delete_key()), and since 7.27.5 it first looks for the key's base (`keys/<key>/.purged`, one access()): a key with a base is moved out of keys/ whole, by a rename(), before it is removed, so a crash never leaves its files without its base or its base without its files. Attributed by reading the code.

ab.label: A page of 1 row, as a replica
ab.meaning: tranger2_iterator_get_page() of one row on a store another yuno writes: what a page costs beyond its rows.
ab.method: The read phase of perf_timeranger2 alone, 48 rounds, the binaries of 7.27.0 and 7.27.5 (and 7.27.4 in the last 24) run in rotation, a sync and a 1 s pause before each run.
ab.reason: check_purge_before_read(): before every iterator open and every page, a replica stat()s the first md2 file of the key, to notice a purge of the master whose signal it did not hear (an overflow of its watch, a follower down while the master purged, a replica without a follower), before the read meets files that are gone. About 1 us per call on this machine, purged or not. Placed by a rotation of every tag from 7.27.0 to 7.27.5 and of two commits of 7.27.5 (24 rounds): 7.27.1 to 7.27.4 and bd3fdce51 read at 7.27.0's speed, and it appears with 83a771089 (the followers hear a purge), the commit that brings the check. On this figure: 7.27.4 5.12 us, bd3fdce51 5.19, 83a771089 6.03, 7.27.5 6.10. Kept: skipping the check while nothing seems missed leaves a window (a signal not yet read from the queue) in which a read opens a deleted file.

ab.method: The read phase of perf_timeranger2 alone, 48 rounds, the binaries of 7.27.0 and 7.27.5 (and 7.27.4 in the last 24) run in rotation, a sync and a 1 s pause before each run.
ab.reason: +1.5% (t = 3.5, 48 rounds). Not the check (1 us over 100 rows is 0.4%): the master's page of 100 rows moves the same way (+1.1%, t = 1.7 here; +2.6% in the rotation of the tags). In the rotation it appears with bd3fdce51, the first commit of 7.27.5 (7.27.4 261.7 us, bd3fdce51 266.4, 7.27.5 265.9): a page of an unfiltered iterator counts its rows as positions among the live rows, g_rowid = purged + position, so the base of a key is read for every row.
